summary: First Lady; John's 4th cousin 7x removed via Tuthill (also 5C6R via Wells).
bio:
Daughter of Anna Tuthill; raised on Long Island by her Tuthill grandparents. Grandmother of President Benjamin Harrison.

Each connecting generation is now sourced from Akerly's Tuthill genealogy ([R4-S1]) and Hayes's Wells genealogy ([R4-S3]): John Tuthill (1635-1717, 12 generations above John) -> Henry Tuthill 'the Justice' (b. 1 May 1665, d. 4 Jan 1750; m. Bethia Horton, daughter of Capt. Jonathan Horton and Bethia, daughter of William Wells) -> Henry (b. 1690, d. 1 Sep 1775) -> Henry (b. before Dec 1715, d. 17 Sep 1793; m. 16 Mar 1738 Phoebe Horton) -> Anna Tuthill (m. John Cleves Symmes) -> Anna. Akerly states outright: 'Henry's grand-da., Anna Symmes, m. President Wm. Henry Harrison, and was the grandmother of President Benjamin Harrison.' Result: 4th cousin 7 times removed via Tuthill and 5th cousin 6 times removed via William Wells, both confirmed generation by generation in compiled sources. A third, conditional route: both Bethia Horton and Phoebe Horton descend from Barnabas Horton, whom Round 3 places 13 generations above John through Rachel Browne (probable); that would add 5C7R twice. Wikipedia ([R4-S2]) notes she was the only First Lady never to visit the capital during her husband's presidency.
sources: [R4-S1] Lucy D. Akerly, The Tuthill Family of Tharston, Norfolk Co., England, and Southold, Suffolk Co., New York (1898) (archive.org full text), pp. 7-10 (secondary) https://archive.org/details/tuthillfamilyoft00aker
[R4-S3] Charles W. Hayes, William Wells of Southold and his Descendants (1878) (archive.org full text), pp. 27-28, 33 (secondary) https://archive.org/details/williamwellsofso00byuhaye

[R4-S4] George F. Horton, Horton Genealogy, or Chronicles of the Descendants of Barnabas Horton (1876) (archive.org full text), pp. 11-12 (secondary) https://archive.org/details/hortongenealogyo00hort

media.title: Wikipedia: Anna Harrison
media.note: Anna Tuthill Harrison (née Symmes; July 25, 1775 – February 25, 1864) was the first lady of the United States in 1841 as the wife of President William Henry Harrison. She served in the role for only one month, as her husband contracted pneumonia and died shortly after his term began.

funFacts: Both First Ladies of the 1840 'Tippecanoe and Tyler Too' ticket are John's cousins: Anna through the Tuthills and Wellses, Julia Gardiner Tyler through Bull Smith.
